prompt: A state government wants to raise its high school graduation rate from 78% to 85%. The candidate's framework: (1) School-level factors: teacher quality and class sizes; (2) Student-level factors: attendance and academic performance; (3) Programs the state already funds. What is the flaw in this framework?

options.text: Buckets 1 and 2 overlap and should be merged
options.feedback: School and student factors are different units of analysis.

options.text: Bucket 1 doesn't matter, since dropouts are a student choice
options.feedback: Teaching and class size affect whether students stay.

options.text: Missing: factors outside school, such as family income, health and the need to work
options.feedback: Right. Out-of-school factors drive many dropouts, and neither bucket covers them.

options.text: It is a generic education framework
options.feedback: The buckets fit graduation. The flaw is the missing out-of-school bucket.

explanation: Dropouts come from school, student and out-of-school factors. The third group, plus the programs available to act on each, is missing.

extras.corrected_framework: School factors; student factors; out-of-school factors; available programs and their cost
